 Nearly 6 million coffee makers recalled after dozens report burn injuries
 By Jason Gunn FOX Local Recalls Published  October 30, 2026 9:55 AM EDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 30, 2026 9:55 AM EDT article Bodum French Press coffee makers with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes (Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper, and Kenya models). Consumer Product Safety Commission. 
 The Brief
 Bodum is recalling approximately 5.9 million of its French press coffee makers after reports that the replaceable glass carafes in certain 8-cup and 12-cup models unexpectedly cracked or shattered during use. 
 According to a recall notice from the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, the glass carafes can break when consumers use metal spoons or other metal utensils to stir coffee. 
 Consumers are urged to stop using metal spoons or utensils to stir coffee inside the glass carafes and contact Bodum to receive a free plastic stirring spoon and warning label. 
 Nearly 6 million French press coffee makers sold at Target, Walmart and other major retailers nationwide are being recalled following dozens of reports of burn injuries.
 What we know:
 Bodum is recalling approximately 5.9 million of its French press coffee makers after reports that the replaceable glass carafes in certain 8-cup and 12-cup models unexpectedly cracked or shattered during use.
 RELATED: Grocer recalls hoagie rolls in seven states over undeclared allergen 
 Dig deeper:
 According to a recall notice from the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, the glass carafes can break when consumers use metal spoons or other metal utensils to stir coffee, posing a burn hazard from hot liquid.
 By the numbers:
 There have been 70 reports of the glass breaking, with 48 people reporting burn injuries. 
 The recall includes Bodum 8-cup and 12-cup Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper and Kenya French press coffee makers equipped with replaceable glass carafes.
 Most affected coffee makers feature the Bodum name on the frame and inside the lid, along with engraved product warnings on the glass carafe.
 RELATED: Feds warn of shock, electrocution risk from brand of pressure washers: Here's what to do 
 Why you should care:
 Consumers are urged to stop using metal spoons or utensils to stir coffee inside the glass carafes and contact Bodum to receive a free plastic stirring spoon and warning label.
 Big picture view:
 The warning label reminds consumers not to use cracked or damaged carafes and warns against stirring coffee with metal utensils, which could cause the glass to break.
 The affected coffee makers were sold through Amazon, Target, Walmart and other retailers nationwide.
 The Source: This story was written with information provided by the Consumer Product Safety Commission. This story was reported from Orlando.
